about: Flags, not bans. A match needs identity.defaults_used[{id, why}] with a brief-grounded why. Section A: model defaults measured 2026-10-02 (180 answers, 30 briefs; claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-4-5). Section B: category cliches in human-made logos. fonts match family names case-insensitively; oklch_regions are [min, max] ranges in OKLCH (L 0-1, C, h degrees), a colour matches when L, C and h all fall inside; logo_tags match identity.logo.tags. Re-measure when models change: an item leaves after two runs under 10%, enters above 25% in any model.

tags.literal-object: the symbol draws the object the brand name names (moon for Moonvault, kestrel for Kestrel Pay)
tags.hidden-letter: an initial or a second meaning hidden inside the symbol
tags.negative-space: the idea depends on a figure read in the empty space
tags.circle-container: symbol enclosed in or built on a circle, ring, disc or badge
tags.local-nod: a landmark, flag or tourist symbol of the brand's city or country
tags.gradient: a gradient fill in the mark or as a brand colour
tags.spark: four-point star or sparkle, 8 vertices with alternating radii
tags.radial-swirl: n rotated copies of one module around a central hole
tags.gradient-orb: a glowing sphere or blob, usually blue-violet
tags.initial-in-rounded-square: one glyph inside a radiused tile that fills most of the canvas
tags.hexagon-nodes: regular hexagon, cube, or node-and-line graph
tags.category-icon: the category's stock icon: leaf, shield, roof, up-arrow, bulb, globe, bolt, mountain, key, flame
tags.swoosh: a generic motion swoosh or orbit arc
tags.outline-icon: icon-set style: stroke-only, stroke about 1/12 of the size, round caps and joins
tags.abstract-geometric: a non-figurative geometric symbol (descriptive tag, not flagged)
tags.letterform: symbol built from the brand's letters in the display face (descriptive tag, not flagged)

entries.note: Display face in 24% of answers, 40% of Opus; read as warm, human, crafted in any sector. Fine when the brief's voice is soft and odd and competitors do not use it.
Text face in 40% of answers (Haiku 57%); fallen into, not chosen. Fine for UI-dense products, wide language needs, an existing Inter brand, or after a side-by-side test.
Cream or bone light neutral in 57-67% of Opus/Sonnet palettes; with terracotta and a serif display in 47-50%.
Terracotta or clay in 63-70% of Opus/Sonnet palettes. Fine when the material is real (fired clay, kraft) or the competitor map shows the region empty.
Gold, brass or mustard accent in 70-77% of Opus/Sonnet palettes, in every sector.

Navy or dark indigo; navy + gold in 27-43% of Opus/Sonnet palettes. Automatic for law, property, finance, insurance, public sector ('trust'). Fine as a deliberate category code when another component carries the difference.
Sector stereotype: wine, hotel, real estate. Same brief gave the same display face 67-80% on repeat, 60% across models.
Sector stereotype: law.
Sector stereotype: construction, logistics.
Sector stereotype: AI, crypto, fintech, security.
Sector stereotype: edtech; also the older-model default display face.

Indigo/violet (#6C5CE7 twice verbatim, Tailwind #6366F1 once) appears only as the technology code: fintech, edtech, crypto, AI. 'Feels like tech' is not a reason. Dark indigo (#0B1026) is caught by navy-primary.

Part of the one logo formula of current models (Moonvault = crescent + vault door, 4 of 4 runs). Fine when the object is distinctive and absent from the competitor shelf, or a non-literal set is shown beside it.
Letter or second meaning inside the symbol: Opus 6/30, Sonnet 15/30.
Negative space named in 23-50% of logo concepts (Sonnet 50%).
Circle, ring or disc in 47-60% of Opus/Sonnet marks.
'A nod to' a local landmark in half of Opus/Sonnet marks, always the tourist symbol.
Rare (5%) but a cliche when it comes, blue to purple above all. Fine when the medium carries it and a flat one-colour master exists.
AI feature icon (Gemini, Photoshop, Grammarly, Wix).
AI product marks.
AI startups; the 'AI gradient'.
The rounded tile is the app-icon container, not a mark. Legitimate as the app-icon version of a real mark.
Dev, cloud and data startups. Legitimate for a name like 'Hex...'.
Eco leaf, security shield, property roof, finance arrow, ideas bulb, logistics globe, energy bolt. Name three category cliches before building.
Generic motion mark.
An icon-set glyph is not a mark; it vanishes among UI icons.
